recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中出現多顆中型、核偏位、染色質粗塊狀、細胞質深藍且有核周淡染區的漿細胞樣細胞，血液中出現這麼多漿細胞應考慮漿細胞白血病。
features: Circulating medium-sized plasma cells with eccentric round nuclei
Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with perinuclear hof in several cells
Chromatin coarse to clumped; nucleoli not conspicuous in most cells
Moderate to high N:C ratio in some cells, with narrow rims of cytoplasm
Background of peripheral red cells without prominent rouleaux in these crops
describe_en: Composite peripheral blood smear images show multiple circulating plasma cells with eccentric round nuclei, coarse clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm, several with a perinuclear hof. Some cells have a higher N:C ratio with a narrow rim of cytoplasm, but distinct large nucleoli typical of plasmablasts are not clearly seen in these crops. Background red cells are unremarkable at this magnification. Findings are consistent with circulating clonal plasma cells as seen in plasma cell leukemia; diagnosis requires enumeration (5% or more circulating plasma cells by current criteria) and confirmation by flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Reactive cells are heterogeneous in size with a spectrum to normal lymphocytes and are polytypic, rather than a monotonous clonal population.
Circulating cells are mostly small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid lymphocytes with MYD88 L265P and CD19/CD20 expression, unlike CD138+/CD38 bright, CD19-negative plasma cells.
Cells are large with prominent central nucleoli and are often EBV-positive, lacking the clumped chromatin seen here.
